extracted.intended_audience: astronomers, astronomical photographers, and scientific researchers working with photographic plates and historical eclipse data
extracted.subtask_description: Diagnosing and preventing photographic irradiation (haloing/‘eating-in’) in over-exposed astronomical plates (notably corona photography), and methods for using historical eclipses to test lunar-motion elements. Covers experimental tests of plate materials/backings and interpretation of inner vs outer irradiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Walker Prize submission rules (Boston Society of Natural History)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two annual prizes offered for the best memoirs, written in English, on subjects proposed by a Committee appointed by the Council. For the best memoir a prize of sixty dollars may be awarded, and if of marked merit the amount may be increased at the Committee's discretion to one hundred dollars; the memoir next in value may receive up to fifty dollars. Neither prize is to be awarded unless the papers under consideration are deemed of adequate merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memoirs must be forwarded prepaid and addressed 'Boston Society of Natural History, for the Committee on the Walker Prizes, Boston, Mass.' on or before April 1, 1873. Each memoir must be accompanied by a sealed envelope enclosing the author's name and subscribed by a motto corresponding to that borne by the manuscript. Example: Annual Prize 1873 subject given as 'On the Development and Transformations of the Common House Fly.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Academy of Caen prize specification (paper on leaves)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prize (4,000 francs) offered for a paper on 'The part played by leaves in vegetation' seeking accounts of exact experiments and new facts calculated to clear up, invalidate, confirm, or modify doubtful points in received theories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers must be sent before December 31, 1875, addressed to M. Travers, secretary of the Academy, Caen. Emphasis on exact experiments and new facts (i.e., empirical, experimental work addressing theoretical uncertainties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of historical eclipses to test lunar-motion elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical solar and lunar eclipses provide important tests of the elements of the moon's motion and of secular acceleration when carried back to remote times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ the latest available values for secular acceleration (e.g., Prof. Hansen's value) and combine with other important elements (e.g., Leverrier's solar tables). Treat ancient eclipses as primary data for constraining lunar motion; small corrections in lunar elements can change whether totality passed over a given site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for historical eclipses used in chronological/astronomical work
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferentially select 'better-known' eclipses—those with reliable, specific historical records (clear locality, time-of-day, and descriptive detail) that can be meaningfully compared with calculated tracks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid records with uncertain circumstances (e.g., unknown sailing direction or vague locality) that reduce scientific value. Use authoritative place coordinates (e.g., those deduced by the Astronomer Royal) for direct calculations of central line, duration, and local times. Report calculated phases, durations, and central-line tracks to judge compatibility with historical accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and characterization of photographic irradiation in over-exposed plates
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographic irradiation: in over-exposed photographs of luminous objects on a dark background, brighter parts are surrounded by a nebulous haze or border of light which increases the apparent diameter of luminous objects at the expense of less luminous parts. The phenomenon varies with exposure time and the relative brightness of object and background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Irradiation manifests as two components in pronounced cases—an inner, sharply defined border following the object's contour, and an outer, less definite haze. The inner border fades gradually outward and is difficult to separate from the true image; the boundary between inner and outer halos is more definite but not absolutely precise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnosis: outer-haze (external halo) source and experimental test
rubrics_metrics.description: The outer irradiation halo is produced by reflections from the back surface of the plate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental tests: (a) Use opaque support (ebonite): outer haze disappears. (b) Use 'non-actinic yellow glass': outer haze is much fainter than on ordinary white glass. (c) Place wetted black paper at back of unground plate: outer haze greatly reduced. (d) Grind both back and front surfaces of yellow glass-plate and cover back with black varnish: outer haze becomes imperceptible. Interpretation: reflections at the back surface produce the outer halo; reducing reflection (via backing or index-matching) removes it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical mitigation for outer irradiation halo
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures to avoid or greatly reduce the outer irradiation halo in over-exposed corona or other photographs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If transmitted-light copying of negatives is not required, avoid outer halo by using opaque plates (e.g., ebonite). If negatives must be transmissible, use transparent glass plates with a backing of wet black paper or black varnish; grinding plate surfaces also helps. These measures reduce back-surface reflections and thus the outer halo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inner-fringe (inner border) attribution and implications
rubrics_metrics.description: The inner, more sharply-marked irradiation edge remains after measures that remove the outer halo, and therefore is not caused by back-surface reflections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the inner fringe persists on opaque and backed plates, its cause must lie in front-of-plate effects—either within the thickness of the collodion layer or due to optical imperfections of the instrument. Mitigation therefore requires attention to collodion preparation, film thickness, or optical instrument quality rather than plate backing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental approach for investigating photographic irradiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic experimental protocol to separate and identify sources of irradiation by varying plate material, backing, and surface treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare over-exposed photographs taken on different supports (ebonite, yellow glass, ordinary white glass) and under identical exposure conditions. Apply backings (wetted black paper, black varnish) and surface treatments (grinding front/back) to observe which halo components change. Use these controlled variations to attribute outer halo to back reflections and inner halo to film/optical factors.
